idiom_name: typed state interface or discriminated union plus a store class with subscribe; framework stores at the boundary
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds a compile-time shape to the same idiom: the screen state is an interface (or a discriminated union of screen states), the presentation model a class or a set of functions over an immutable state object with command methods, and the view re-renders after subscribe callbacks - the compiler verifies what the view may read and which commands exist, but nothing binds at runtime, so synchronization is still explicit or delegated to a store library. A discriminated union makes impossible screens unrepresentable (loading/ready/error as variants), which is the type-level contribution to the pattern. Keep the model free of DOM types so it can be constructed in a plain node test environment.
pitfalls: Structural typing does not guarantee the runtime shape: data arriving from the network needs validation, or the view trusts a state object the model never produced.
Types are erased, so the discriminated union prevents nothing at runtime and immutability discipline remains the developer's job - in-place mutation does not re-render.
Class-field initialisation runs before the constructor body for ES2022 targets, so fields can overwrite values assigned during construction; the handbook documents this initialisation-order trap.
Extracting a method as a callback loses the receiver unless it is bound, and TypeScript's this-typing will reject the call rather than silently misbehave.
